🚨🌎 COLOMBIA'S FAR-RIGHT TAKES FIRST ROUND — REGIONAL PROGRESSIVE BLOC TESTED

Milei-aligned outsider Abelardo de la Espriella took 43.74% (10.36M votes) Sunday, edging Pacto Histórico's Iván Cepeda (40.90%, 9.69M). VOX's Abascal and Ecuador's Noboa congratulated De la Espriella the same night. June 21 second round will decide. The Latin American right is networking openly — and the regional bloc Sheinbaum, Lula and Petro have been holding together just got its hardest test in a year.

Source: jornada.com.mx

🇲🇽🏭 <u>RECORD $4.52B APRIL SURPLUS — EXPORTS UP 32.6%, NON-AUTO MANUFACTURING +45.8%</u>

Mexico's trade surplus hit $4.520 billion in April, ~10x the $476 million Bloomberg consensus, El Financiero reports. Exports reached $72.042 billion — the highest single-month figure since INEGI began records in 1980 — pulled by non-automotive manufacturing growth of 45.8% annual. Jan–April surplus stands at $3.508 billion, against a $314 million deficit in the same period of 2025. The US absorbed 83.6% of those exports. Trump's tariff wall is not delivering what was advertised.

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>PEMEX DEBT DOWN $20B, 1.3M BARRELS/DAY — MEXICO'S FUEL HOLDS WHILE WORLD BURNS</u>

Sheinbaum, defending the Olmeca/Dos Bocas refinery, the Deer Park purchase in Texas, and the rebuilt coker units at Tula and Salina Cruz: "We rescued Pemex and CFE as true companies of the people." Pemex has cut $20 billion in debt while processing 1.3 million barrels per day. CFE has added 3,000 MW from six new combined-cycle plants since the sexenio began, with 32,000 MW more queued and renewables programmed to climb from 24% to 38%. While oil markets convulse over Hormuz, Mexican families pay yesterday's price for gasoline and diesel.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>US IS 100% IMPORT-DEPENDENT ON MEXICO FOR 3 CRITICAL MINERALS</u>

Mexico produces over 60 minerals. Nine are on Trump's "critical" list. The US depends on Mexico for 100% of its fluorite, graphite, and strontium imports — plus 77% of silver, 75%+ of barite, 73% of zinc, 57% of refined copper. Trump's "Pax Silica" framework gathered 54 countries on February 4 to lock down supply chains against China; the US Eximbank put up $10 billion for the Vault Project and another $14.8 billion in Letters of Interest. The mineral war is on, and Mexico holds cards Washington needs.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>PAN-LINKED LBR & GCAM EXPOSED — US INTERFERENCE OP AGAINST SHEINBAUM</u>

Contralínea names the operation: law firm León Barrena Rodríguez (LBR), founded late 2025, and US-based Grey Catalyst Asset Management (GCAM), running disinformation against Sheinbaum and Morena from San Francisco to Mexico City via Substack newsletters and social campaigns. The thread runs through PAN's Santiago Creel and J Hank Rhon III, targeting Mexican consulates with unsubstantiated corruption allegations. Their own copy gives the game away: they will defend "free markets" while Mexico "stubbornly clings to obsolete principles of non-intervention." That is the confession.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>"MEXICO IS NOBODY'S PIÑATA" — SHEINBAUM RIPS US INTERFERENCE</u>

Before 130,000 at the Monumento a la Revolución, Sheinbaum said it is "legitimate to doubt" US intentions when Washington dictates extradition trials, names 10 Mexican officials including ex-Sinaloa governor Rocha Moya, and runs operations in Chihuahua that left two US agents dead. "When external actors decide who is guilty and who is not, we are no longer talking about cooperation — we are talking about interference." She floated the obvious: US sectors positioning for their 2026 midterms, or trying to bend Mexico's 2027 vote.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>12 CABINET MINISTERS EARN MORE THAN SHEINBAUM — ARTICLE 127 IGNORED</u>

Of 15 secretaries who filed 2026 declarations, 12 reported 2025 net salaries above the president's, in apparent violation of Article 127 of the Constitution. Sheinbaum reported 1.79 million pesos net; Science Secretary Rosaura Ruiz reported 3.011 million — nearly double. Only Rosa Icela Rodríguez (Gobernación), Roberto Velasco (SRE), and infrastructure chief Esteva Medina were under the cap. The austerity republic is policed at the top before anywhere else.

🇲🇽✊ Sheinbaum at the Monument to the Revolution today: "In 1992, Salinas privatized our water rights — opening them to commercial trade. It led to hoarding and corruption." "With the new National Waters Law, we brought them back to the nation. We de-privatized 4.6 billion cubic meters of water that had been concentrated in a few hands." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo Tijuana, Mexicali, and small campesinos got their rights restored. Neoliberalism, line by line, being undone.

🔥🇲🇽 Sheinbaum drew the line at the Monument to the Revolution: "A sellout right, willing to celebrate and even promote pressure from foreign politicians. A right that goes so far as to invite the Spanish far-right to pay tribute to Hernán Cortés. Commentators who travel abroad to speak badly of Mexico." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo 500 years later, the Mexican opposition is still siding with the conquistador.

🇲🇽🏭 The numbers Sheinbaum read out at the Monument to the Revolution today: — Peso at 17.40 to the dollar, up from 19.65 a year ago. Second-most-appreciated currency on Earth against the dollar. — Record foreign direct investment: $23.591 billion in Q1 2026, +10.4% YoY. — Unemployment at 2.5% — among the three lowest in the world. — 669,000 new jobs. April 2026 the highest formal employment month in Mexican history. — Trade balance positive for the first time in many years. — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo, dos años del triunfo This is what an economy looks like when it isn't run from abroad.
